```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.6, dpi = 120)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
source("pld_validation.R", local = TRUE)
load("../../data/cod_obs.rda")
root <- normalizePath(params$results, mustWork = TRUE)
roots <- if (nzchar(params$extra_results)) {
  c(root, normalizePath(params$extra_results, mustWork = TRUE))
} else root
arms <- c("Lognormal", "Survey PLD", "Catch PLD", "Both PLD",
  "Fixed detection", "No occurrence")
scenario_labels <- c(exact = "Exact PLD", multinomial = "Varying age samples",
  low = "Low effort", standard = "Standard effort", high = "High effort")
read_runs <- function(pattern) {
  files <- unlist(lapply(roots, list.files, pattern = pattern, full.names = TRUE), use.names = FALSE)
  # The latest result from extra_results takes precedence over pilots.
  files <- files[!duplicated(basename(files), fromLast = TRUE)]
  setNames(lapply(files, readRDS), sub("[.]rds$", "", basename(files)))
}
inputs <- read_runs("^(controlled|sampling)-[0-9]+[.]rds$")
fits <- read_runs("^fit-(controlled|sampling)-[0-9]+-.*[.]rds$")
fit_status <- bind_rows(lapply(names(fits), function(name) {
  a <- fits[[name]]
  keys <- strsplit(sub("^fit-", "", name), "-", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  data.frame(attempt = name, design = keys[1], history = as.integer(keys[2]),
    scenario = keys[3], resolution = as.integer(sub("a", "", keys[4])),
    model = arms[as.integer(sub("model", "", keys[5]))],
    success = isTRUE(a$value$converged), warnings = length(a$warnings),
    error = a$error, elapsed = a$elapsed)
}))
if (!length(fits)) {
  fit_status <- data.frame(attempt = character(), design = character(), history = integer(),
    scenario = character(), resolution = integer(), model = character(),
    success = logical(), warnings = integer(), error = character(), elapsed = numeric())
}
summarise_fit <- function(name) {
  if (!length(fits)) return(data.frame())
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(fit_status)), function(i) {
    row <- fit_status[i, ]
    if (!row$success) return(NULL)
    table <- fits[[row$attempt]]$value$metric[[name]]
    cbind(row[c("design", "scenario", "history", "resolution", "model")], table)
  }))
}
annual <- summarise_fit("annual")
scale_check <- data.frame()
if (nrow(annual)) {
  annual <- mutate(annual, log_error = log(est / truth),
    covered = if_else(is.finite(lwr) & is.finite(upr), truth >= lwr & truth <= upr, NA))
  scale_check <- annual |>
    filter(quantity == "ssb") |>
    group_by(design, scenario, resolution, history, model) |>
    summarise(ssb_ratio = median(est / truth), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(outside_scale = !is.finite(ssb_ratio) | ssb_ratio < 0.1 | ssb_ratio > 10)
  annual <- left_join(annual, select(scale_check, -ssb_ratio),
    by = c("design", "scenario", "resolution", "history", "model"))
}
pulse <- summarise_fit("pulse")
if (nrow(pulse)) {
  pulse <- mutate(pulse, height_error = height - height_truth,
    center_error = center - center_truth) |>
    left_join(select(scale_check, -ssb_ratio),
      by = c("design", "scenario", "resolution", "history", "model"))
}
paired <- if (nrow(annual)) {
  key <- group_by(annual, design, scenario, resolution, model, history, quantity)
  metric <- summarise(key, mae = mean(abs(log_error)),
    mean_error = mean(log_error), coverage = mean(covered, na.rm = TRUE),
    finite_intervals = sum(!is.na(covered)), .groups = "drop")
  base <- filter(metric, model == "Lognormal") |>
    select(design, scenario, resolution, history, quantity, baseline = mae)
  inner_join(filter(metric, model %in% arms[2:4]), base,
    by = c("design", "scenario", "resolution", "history", "quantity")) |>
    mutate(difference = mae - baseline)
} else data.frame()
main <- filter(fit_status, resolution == 14L, model %in% arms[1:4])
successful <- sum(main$success)
n_controlled <- sum(startsWith(names(inputs), "controlled-") & vapply(inputs, `[[`, FALSE, "ok"))
n_sampling <- sum(startsWith(names(inputs), "sampling-") & vapply(inputs, `[[`, FALSE, "ok"))
n_input_failures <- sum(!vapply(inputs, `[[`, FALSE, "ok"))
sampling <- lapply(inputs[startsWith(names(inputs), "sampling-")], function(x) x$value)
sampling <- Filter(Negate(is.null), sampling)
design <- if (length(sampling)) sampling[[1L]]$design else NULL
uses_cod_benchmark <- !is.null(design)
if (is.null(design)) {
  design <- list(effort = data.frame(sets_per_1000 = c(1, 2, 4),
    operation_coverage = c(.15, .30, .60)), rv_tow_area = .03)
}
completed_sampling_fits <- sum(fit_status$design == "sampling")
sampling_target_fits <- 24L * 3L * 4L + 8L * 4L
sampling_complete <- n_sampling == 24L && completed_sampling_fits == sampling_target_fits
show_not_ready <- function() knitr::asis_output("No successful fits are available for this comparison.")
label_scenario <- function(x) factor(unname(scenario_labels[x]), levels = scenario_labels)
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11))
compare_height <- function(which_scenario, first = "Lognormal", second = "Both PLD") {
  if (!nrow(pulse)) return(data.frame())
  on_case <- filter(pulse, scenario == which_scenario, resolution == 14L)
  one <- filter(on_case, model == first) |> select(history, baseline = height_error)
  two <- filter(on_case, model == second) |> select(history, alternative = height_error)
  inner_join(one, two, by = "history") |>
    mutate(across(c(baseline, alternative), abs), difference = alternative - baseline)
}
paired_interval <- function(x) {
  if (nrow(x) < 2L) return(rep(NA_real_, 2L))
  se <- sd(x$difference) / sqrt(nrow(x))
  mean(x$difference) + c(-1, 1) * qt(.975, nrow(x) - 1L) * se
}
paired_sentence <- function(x, description) {
  if (!nrow(x)) return("")
  bounds <- paired_interval(x)
  effect <- if (all(is.finite(bounds))) {
    sprintf(" (paired change %+.3f, 95%% Monte Carlo interval [%+.3f, %+.3f])",
      mean(x$difference), bounds[1L], bounds[2L])
  } else ""
  label <- if (nrow(x) == 1L) paste("For one paired successful", description, "history") else {
    sprintf("Across %d paired successful %s histories", nrow(x), description)
  }
  sprintf("%s, mean absolute pulse-height error was %.3f versus %.3f per year%s.",
    label, mean(x$baseline), mean(x$alternative), effect)
}
exact_result <- compare_height("exact")
sampling_result <- compare_height("standard")
exact_sentence <- paired_sentence(exact_result, "exact PLD")
sampling_sentence <- paired_sentence(sampling_result, "standard-effort SimSurvey")
multinomial_sentence <- paired_sentence(compare_height("multinomial"), "variable-effort multinomial")
ablation_sentence <- paired_sentence(compare_height("exact", "No occurrence", "Fixed detection"),
  "fixed-scale exact PLD")
conclusion <- if (!nrow(exact_result)) {
  "Assessment recovery remains untested in these outputs."
} else if (!nrow(sampling_result)) {
  "The controlled recovery comparison evaluates the value of zeros when the model describes sampling. The SimSurvey assessment comparison remains incomplete."
} else {
  delta <- paired_interval(sampling_result)
  if (all(is.finite(delta)) && delta[2L] < 0) {
    "The standard-effort SimSurvey comparison also favoured PLD on the histories where both models passed the numerical checks."
  } else if (all(is.finite(delta)) && delta[1L] > 0) {
    "The standard-effort SimSurvey comparison favoured the positive-only model on the histories where both models passed the numerical checks."
  } else {
    "The standard-effort SimSurvey comparison gave limited evidence that PLD changed mortality recovery. The result applies to the simulated mortality pulse and monitoring designs."
  }
}
```

## Abstract

Catch and survey indices can contain zeros when fish are present but none
appear in a sample. Excluding those records may remove information about weak
cohorts, especially when high mortality leaves few older fish. We tested a
Poisson-link delta lognormal model that uses the predicted observation to
explain both detection and the size of a positive record. We compared it with
the positive-only lognormal using exact PLD draws, age samples with varying
effort, and whole-area Gillnet and RV monitoring in SimSurvey. All scenarios
used the same prescribed natural-mortality pulse.
`r if (uses_cod_benchmark) "We used Northern cod's recorded zero frequencies to calibrate standard SimSurvey monitoring."`
This report includes
`r n_controlled` controlled and `r n_sampling` SimSurvey histories, and
`r successful` of `r nrow(main)` checkpointed main 14+ attempts passed numerical
checks.
`r exact_sentence` `r multinomial_sentence` `r sampling_sentence` `r conclusion`

## Why can a zero help?

The SimSurvey run is `r if (sampling_complete) "complete" else "in progress"`.
This report includes `r n_sampling` of the 24 planned histories and
`r completed_sampling_fits` of `r sampling_target_fits` planned fit attempts
to this copy. Diagnostics and scores use the simulated observations provided
to each fit. There is no held-out prediction experiment.

For a predicted arithmetic mean \(\widetilde Y\), the probability that the
observed value \(Y\) is zero is
\[
p_0 = P(Y=0) = 2^{-\widetilde Y/\widetilde Y_{50}} .
\]
The half-detection level \(\widetilde Y_{50}\) has the same units as the
observations. The positive component has arithmetic mean
\(\widetilde Y/(1-p_0)\) and log-SD \(\sigma\). Its log median is
\(\log\{\widetilde Y/(1-p_0)\}-\sigma^2/2\). The
legacy lognormal uses the population prediction as the median and omits
zeros. The fits therefore differ both in their treatment of zeros and in how
they interpret a positive number. The exact simulation also compares two
fits with fixed true \(\widetilde Y_{50}\) and the same positive density. Omitting just
the detection contribution from one fit isolates the direct information
from occurrence.

## What was simulated?

Natural mortality increased from 0.25 to 0.60 per year during years 5-9,
stayed high through year 12, and returned to 0.25 by year 16. Fishing was
held at a reference peak F of 0.06 with a normal-shaped age curve (peak 7.7,
width 2.5 years). Recruitment used SimSurvey defaults and separate random
streams for each history. Coverage extended to the whole simulation grid.
RV catchability rose with age using SimSurvey's default logistic curve.
TinyAM estimated both curves and one shared annual AR(1) M state across
ages, with exact cohort survival and random-walk recruitment. The same
settings and default optimization controls were used across observation
models.

SimSurvey's default maturity depends on length. To preserve its expected
mature biomass in tinyAM, maturity at age was calculated as expected
mature weight divided by expected stock weight at age.

The controlled PLD simulation drew independent observations from the fitted
family. The age-sampling scenario drew multinomial samples within each
year and expanded each sample to the known total. It preserved the same
expected value at each age and introduced a shared total, correlated
age estimates, and changing sample sizes. The sample-size multiplier
cycled through 0.5, 1, 2 and 1 independently of the mortality phases.
At age 14+ the controlled simulation used the fitted model's plus-group
survival from year 2.

In the SimSurvey runs, all three effort levels reused the same realized
fishery catches. The Gillnet program monitored
`r paste(scales::percent(design$effort$operation_coverage, accuracy = 1), collapse = ", ")` of operations
and aged up to 150 fish per monitored operation at random. Each simulated
operation represented a bundle of 1,200 nets. This makes operation-level
resampling practical. It also makes the sampling unit a cluster and
reduces the number of sampling opportunities compared with small sets. The RV survey
sampled `r paste(design$effort$sets_per_1000, collapse = ", ")` sets per
1,000 square kilometres, with at least two sets per stratum. Each tow swept
`r format(design$rv_tow_area, digits = 3, scientific = FALSE)` square kilometres.
It measured up to 100 lengths per set and aged up to three fish
per 3-cm group and set. Age-length key estimation and stratified expansion
produce the observed index. Missing coverage and unsupported age estimates
were recorded as missing. Both programs retained supported zeros. [SimSurvey
methods](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0232822)

```{r calibration-design, results='asis'}

  cat(paste("We calibrated the standard monitoring effort to the fraction of observed ages",
    "recorded as zero in Northern cod. We changed the share of fishing operations",
    "monitored and the area swept per RV tow. The survey estimator expands catches",
    "by the inverse of swept area, so reducing the footprint lowers rare-age",
    "encounters while preserving the whole-area index target before age subsampling.",
    "The biological histories, prescribed mortality, selectivity and calendar of",
    "sampling effort were held fixed. The cod case guides the overall prevalence of",
    "zeros. Its age and year patterns also reflect stock and monitoring histories",
    "that differ from this experiment. The RV footprint is an effective sampling",
    "setting. The first study used 0.03 square kilometres per tow. The calibrated",
    "study explores fewer encounters per tow at the same number of stations.",
    "We piloted four footprints across three histories spanning low to high",
    "recruitment and compared fishery coverage settings by replaying existing",
    "operations. We selected the final settings from these observation patterns",

```{r swept-area-audit, results='asis'}
if (uses_cod_benchmark) {
  survey_audit <- bind_rows(lapply(sampling, function(history) {
    bind_rows(lapply(history$series, function(program) {
      target <- filter(program$expected_index, age >= 2L)
      caught <- filter(program$survey_caught, age >= 2L)
      data.frame(effort = program$effort$effort, target = sum(target$mu),
        expanded = sum(caught$expanded) / 1000)
    }))
  }))
  ratios <- survey_audit |>
    group_by(effort) |>
    summarise(ratio = sum(expanded) / sum(target), .groups = "drop")
  standard <- filter(ratios, effort == "standard")$ratio
  if (length(standard) && standard > 0) {
    cat(sprintf("Before length and age subsampling, expanding the catches with their exact ages gave %.1f%% of the known total RV index at standard effort (simulated ages 2-20, summed over years and histories). This checks the swept-area adjustment against the known abundance times catchability.",
      100 * standard))
  }
}
```

The study used a private copy of the pinned SimSurvey fisheries routine
that batches the multinomial allocation of lengths to cells. It retains the
same sampling law and cell-age totals while changing random-number order.
The recorded catches, operation controls and estimator come from SimSurvey.
[Pinned fishery source](https://github.com/PaulRegular/SimSurvey/blob/29a1b03350c274f88dac108fb95f9446eac79233/R/fishery_engine.R)

### Where did the zeros occur?

The Northern cod benchmark uses commercial catch and Fall 2J3KL RV
observations from 1983-2025. Comparisons use ages 2-14+ in both data sets.
The simulated fits also use age 1. A recorded zero counts as an observation.
Years or ages with missing records are excluded from the zero frequency.

```{r cod-zero-benchmark, fig.width=9, fig.cap="Zero frequency by modeled age in SimSurvey and the Northern cod example. The black line shows Northern cod in 1983-2025, ages 2-14+. Each coloured line averages over the available observations from the simulated histories at one sampling effort. In both data sets, age 14 includes ages 14-20 and missing observations are excluded from the denominator."}
# Keep the observation keys when summing across age groups with differing
# formula covariates.
cod_inputs <- lapply(cod_obs[c("catch", "index")], function(x) x[c("year", "age", "obs")])
cod <- pld_cod_observation_rows(cod_inputs)
if (length(sampling)) {
  comparable_zeros <- bind_rows(cod, filter(pld_sim_observation_rows(sampling), age >= 2L)) |>

```{r cod-zero-benchmark-totals, results='asis'}
if (length(sampling)) {

```

The commercial catch and survey have different age patterns. Northern cod
catch includes many zeros at age 2 and few in the middle of the age range.
The RV survey zeros occur at older ages. The same overall percentage can
therefore imply different information about the cohorts affected by the
mortality increase.

Age 14+ sums the records at ages 14-20 before fitting. A positive value
therefore can include an age that had no recorded fish, even with PLD.
Comparison with age 20+ changes both the number of zero cells and the time
fish can remain in the terminal age. The 14+ model also uses age-14 mortality
and catchability throughout the bin. SimSurvey applies the native curves
and lets fish exit at age 20. The two resolutions cannot be compared by
information criteria.

```{r plus-selectivity, fig.cap="Percent difference between effective age-14+ selectivity or catchability and the generating value at age 14. Each line is one completed history. Zero marks the age-14 value. The panels have different vertical scales because the survey logistic curve is nearly flat at these ages."}
if (length(sampling)) {
  plus_selectivity <- bind_rows(lapply(sampling, function(x) {
    ages <- filter(x$reference, age >= 14L)
    # Baranov catch is linear in F at the prescribed Z; use each native age's
    # abundance and year-specific fraction exposed to fishing as weights.
    ages |>
      mutate(catch_weight = N * (-expm1(-Z)) / Z,
        q = stats::plogis(2 * (age - 3))) |>
      group_by(year) |>
      summarise(Gillnet = weighted.mean(selectivity, catch_weight) / selectivity[age == 14L],
        RV = weighted.mean(q, N) / q[age == 14L], .groups = "drop") |>
      mutate(history = x$id)
  })) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Gillnet, RV), names_to = "program", values_to = "ratio")
  ggplot(plus_selectivity, aes(year, 100 * (ratio - 1), group = history)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) + geom_line(alpha = .55, colour = "#126782") +
    facet_wrap(~program, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(x = "Year", y = "Difference from the age-14 value (%)")
}
```

```{r plus-selectivity-summary, results='asis'}
if (length(sampling)) {
  ranges <- plus_selectivity |>
    group_by(program) |>
    summarise(minimum = min(ratio), maximum = max(ratio), .groups = "drop")
  gillnet <- filter(ranges, program == "Gillnet")
  rv <- filter(ranges, program == "RV")
  cat(sprintf("Effective Gillnet selectivity was %.1f-%.1f%% of age-14 selectivity. Effective RV catchability exceeded age-14 catchability by %.2g-%.2g%%.",
    100 * gillnet$minimum, 100 * gillnet$maximum,
    100 * (rv$minimum - 1), 100 * (rv$maximum - 1)))
}
```

The catch summary weights native selectivity by \(N_a(1-e^{-Z_a})/Z_a\).
At the simulator's prescribed \(Z_a\), that choice reproduces the total
reference Baranov catch for ages 14-20. Survey catchability is weighted by
abundance at the start of the year, when the survey takes place. The
comparison uses generating curves and simulated abundances, with no
assumption about which ages appeared in a particular sample.

## What F and M did the simulator generate?

```{r mortality-truth, fig.cap="Simulated fishing mortality (F) and natural mortality (M) through time, averaged over ages 5-10 using abundance at age. The prescribed rates determine survival. Realized F follows the catches allocated by SimSurvey, and realized M is the remainder of prescribed total mortality. Thin lines show individual histories. Thick lines show medians."}
if (length(sampling)) {
  mortality <- bind_rows(lapply(sampling, function(x) mutate(x$reference, history = x$id)))
  audit <- mortality |>
    filter(age %in% 5:10, is.finite(M_realized)) |>
    group_by(history, year) |>
    summarise(M_ref = weighted.mean(M_reference, N),
      M_real = weighted.mean(M_realized, N), F_ref = weighted.mean(F_reference, N),
      F_real = weighted.mean(F_realized, N), .groups = "drop")
  rates <- audit |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(c(F_ref, F_real, M_ref, M_real), names_to = c("parameter", "source"),
      names_sep = "_", values_to = "rate") |>
    mutate(parameter = recode(parameter, F = "Fishing mortality (F)", M = "Natural mortality (M)"),
      source = factor(source, levels = c("ref", "real"), labels = c("Prescribed", "Realized")))
  medians <- rates |>
    group_by(parameter, source, year) |>
    summarise(rate = median(rate), .groups = "drop")
  ggplot(rates, aes(year, rate, colour = source, linetype = source)) +
    geom_line(aes(group = interaction(history, source)), alpha = .25) +
    geom_line(data = medians, linewidth = .9) + facet_wrap(~parameter, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(Prescribed = "#383838", Realized = "#126782")) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(Prescribed = "dashed", Realized = "solid")) +
    labs(x = "Year", y = "Abundance-weighted rate (per year)", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL)
}
```

```{r mortality-by-age, fig.width=9, fig.height=5.6, fig.cap="Simulated fishing mortality (top) and natural mortality (bottom) by age and year. Prescribed rates on the left generate the population histories. Realized rates on the right are medians across histories at each age and year. Within each row the colour scale is shared between the two panels."}
if (length(sampling)) {
  surfaces <- mortality |>
    select(year, age, F_reference, F_realized, M_reference, M_realized) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(year, age), names_to = c("parameter", "source"),
      names_sep = "_", values_to = "rate") |>
    group_by(year, age, parameter, source) |>
    summarise(rate = median(rate, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(source = factor(source, levels = c("reference", "realized"),
      labels = c("Prescribed", "Realized")))
  draw_surface <- function(which_rate, title) {
    ggplot(filter(surfaces, parameter == which_rate), aes(year, age, fill = rate)) +
      geom_tile() + facet_wrap(~source) +
      scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Per year", option = "cividis") +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 5, 10, 15, 20), expand = c(0, .5)) +
      scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(1, 5, 10, 15, 20), expand = c(0, .5)) +
      labs(x = "Year", y = "Age", title = title)
  }
  grid::grid.newpage()
  grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout = grid::grid.layout(2, 1)))
  print(draw_surface("F", "Fishing mortality (F)"), vp = grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 1))
  print(draw_surface("M", "Natural mortality (M)"), vp = grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 2))
  grid::popViewport()
}
```

  pulses <- audit |>

The greatest year-end loss beyond age 20 across these histories was %.3f%% of total beginning-of-year abundance.",
    sum(ledger$shortfall > 0), nrow(ledger), max(abs(audit$M_real - audit$M_ref)),

    mean(audit$F_ref), mean(audit$F_real), mean(audit$M_ref), mean(audit$M_real)))

When F is small, fitted catch is approximately (NF). The index also
depends on the product (Nq). Multiplying abundance and dividing F and q
by nearly the same factor can therefore leave observation predictions
similar. Here the biomass audit uses simulation truth to flag this
confounding. It would be harder to recognize from observations alone.
Recovery figures retain these attempts and a separate comparison below
shows how the scale flag affects the common set. A passed numerical check
is a statement about the optimization and local curvature.

```{r detection, fig.cap="Observed and predicted zero frequency across fitted probability bins, calculated for supported rows of successful fits with both data streams using PLD. The dashed diagonal marks equality. These are checks on the fitted data."}

    measures <- common |>
      group_by(scenario, model) |>
      summarise(pairs = n(), legacy = mean(abs(legacy_error)), alternative = mean(abs(height_error)),
        clean_pairs = sum(unflagged), legacy_clean = partial_mae(legacy_error[unflagged]),
        alternative_clean = partial_mae(height_error[unflagged]), .groups = "drop")
    tidyr::expand_grid(scenario = c("low", "standard", "high"), model = arms[1:4]) |>
      left_join(measures, by = c("scenario", "model")) |>
      mutate(scenario = label_scenario(scenario), across(c(pairs, clean_pairs), ~ coalesce(.x, 0L))) |>
      knitr::kable(digits = 3, col.names = c("Effort", "Family", "Pairs", "Lognormal MAE",
        "Family MAE", "Unflagged pairs", "Lognormal MAE (unflagged)", "Family MAE (unflagged)"),
        caption = "Paired mean absolute pulse-height errors (per year) for each 14+ SimSurvey family and the lognormal benchmark.",
        format = "pipe") |>
      print()
  } else show_not_ready()
} else show_not_ready()
```

Each family row uses its own common successful histories with the
lognormal. In the lognormal rows, a successful fit is paired with itself
to show the benchmark's available sample and error. The unflagged columns
use only pairs where both fits' median annual SSB was within a factor of
ten of truth. Small or empty paired samples give little basis for ranking
the families.
The paired PLD recovery results are conditional on eligible sampled zeros
for each series with an estimated detection level, and both fits passing
the numerical checks. The attempted-fit totals include the excluded
histories.

### How well were older ages recovered?

Ages 10-13 cover the older fish immediately below the 14+ group. Each
retains its own abundance estimate in both age resolutions and can be
compared with the corresponding native-age abundance in SimSurvey. From
the saved fit checkpoints, recover fitted abundance by inverting the
single-fleet Baranov catch equation,
\[
\widehat N_{a,t}
=\frac{\widetilde C_{a,t}\widehat Z_{a,t}}
{\widehat F_{a,t}(1-e^{-\widehat Z_{a,t}})},\qquad
\widehat Z_{a,t}=\widehat F_{a,t}+\widehat M_t.
\]
Here \(\widetilde C_{a,t}\) is the catch prediction from the population
equation, before any adjustment for detection or lognormal variance. The
fitted model shares one M at all ages each year. SimSurvey truth is the
number of fish at each native age at the beginning of the year, converted
to thousands of fish to match the fit. The comparison uses identical
age-year cells with finite, positive fitted catches, F, Z and abundances
in each pair. No abundance uncertainty was reconstructed.

```{r older-abundance, fig.cap="Older-age recovery in the 14+ SimSurvey fits. Each point is one numerically successful pair, compared on the same valid age-year cells at ages 10-13. Values below zero favour the indicated PLD family over the lognormal. Open points flag a more than tenfold overall SSB scale error in at least one fit."}
older_paired <- data.frame()
older_fits <- filter(fit_status, design == "sampling", resolution == 14L, success)
if (nrow(older_fits)) {
  older <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(older_fits)), function(i) {
    row <- older_fits[i, ]
    fit <- fits[[row$attempt]]$value
    truth <- inputs[[sprintf("sampling-%02d", row$history)]]$value$reference
    catch <- transmute(filter(fit$obs$catch, age %in% 10:13), year, age, catch = pred)
    fishing <- transmute(filter(fit$metric$F, age %in% 10:13), year, age, F = est)
    natural <- transmute(filter(fit$metric$annual, quantity == "M_bar"), year, M = est)
    numbers <- transmute(filter(truth, age %in% 10:13), year, age, truth = N / 1000)
    inner_join(catch, fishing, by = c("year", "age")) |>
      inner_join(natural, by = "year") |>
      inner_join(numbers, by = c("year", "age")) |>
      mutate(Z = F + M) |>
      filter(if_all(c(catch, F, Z, truth), ~ is.finite(.x) & .x > 0)) |>
      mutate(log_est = log(catch) + log(Z) - log(F) - log(-expm1(-Z)),
        est = exp(log_est)) |>
      filter(is.finite(est), est > 0) |>
      transmute(year, age, error = abs(log_est - log(truth)),
        history = row$history, scenario = row$scenario, model = row$model)
  }))
  if (nrow(older)) {
    baseline <- filter(older, model == "Lognormal") |>
      select(scenario, history, year, age, baseline = error)
    older_paired <- filter(older, model %in% arms[2:4]) |>
      inner_join(baseline, by = c("scenario", "history", "year", "age")) |>
      group_by(scenario, history, model) |>
      summarise(difference = mean(error - baseline), cells = n(), .groups = "drop")
  }
}
if (nrow(older_paired)) {
  flags <- filter(scale_check, design == "sampling", resolution == 14L)
  baseline_flag <- filter(flags, model == "Lognormal") |>
    select(scenario, history, baseline_flag = outside_scale)
  older_paired |>
    left_join(select(flags, scenario, history, model, outside_scale),
      by = c("scenario", "history", "model")) |>
    left_join(baseline_flag, by = c("scenario", "history")) |>
    mutate(scale = if_else(outside_scale | baseline_flag, "Scale flag", "Within tenfold")) |>
    ggplot(aes(difference, model, shape = scale)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0, height = .12, alpha = .75) +
    facet_wrap(~label_scenario(scenario)) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c("Scale flag" = 1, "Within tenfold" = 16)) +
    labs(x = "Change in mean absolute log-abundance error", y = NULL, shape = "SSB check")
} else show_not_ready()
```

```{r older-abundance-support, results='asis'}
if (nrow(older_paired)) {
  cat(sprintf("The figure includes %d paired comparisons, with %d to %d common age-year cells per pair.",
    nrow(older_paired), min(older_paired$cells), max(older_paired$cells)))
}
```

```{r fishing, fig.cap="Age profile of F in successful 14+ fits. Points show median fitted F across years and histories. The dashed line shows the normal curve used for generating reference F. The pooled age is omitted because the two curves refer to different quantities there."}
fishing <- summarise_fit("F")
if (nrow(fishing)) {
  fishing |>
    filter(resolution == 14L, model %in% arms[1:4]) |>
    group_by(model, scenario, age) |>
    summarise(F = median(est), F_ref = first(truth), .groups = "drop") |>
    ggplot(aes(age, F, colour = model)) + geom_line() +
    geom_line(aes(y = F_ref), colour = "black", linetype = 2) +
    facet_wrap(~label_scenario(scenario)) + labs(x = "Age", y = "F (per year)", colour = "Fit")
}
```

```{r weak-cohorts, fig.cap="Mean absolute log error of weak cohorts, defined within each generating history as the five lowest recruitment years. Each point is one successful fit."}
if (nrow(annual)) {
  annual |>
    filter(quantity == "recruitment", resolution == 14L, model %in% arms[1:4]) |>
    group_by(scenario, history, model) |>
    slice_min(truth, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    summarise(error = mean(abs(log_error)), .groups = "drop") |>
    ggplot(aes(model, error)) + geom_jitter(width = .12, alpha = .5) +
    facet_wrap(~label_scenario(scenario)) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Weak-cohort log error")
}
```

## Interpretation

The comparison of survey-only, catch-only and joint fits separates the
consequences of modeling nondetection in the two data streams. Detection
calibration helps distinguish a useful occurrence relationship from a
numerically acceptable fit. The fixed-scale ablation addresses the additional
question of whether the Bernoulli contribution itself improves the pulse
estimate once the positive density is held constant.

Every simulated history has the same true M pulse and a fixed reference F
curve. Estimating false-pulse rates would require histories without a
pulse. Testing whether the fits can separate a change in M from a change
in F would require independently varying both rates.

A constant half-detection scale describes one effective observation process.
In real monitoring, sampling effort and the allocation of age samples may
alter the chance of a zero at the same expected index or catch. The
multinomial and SimSurvey comparisons test that limitation. Plus-group
aggregation, a one-parameter occurrence curve and repeated ages from the same
sample also limit interpretation. Treat numerical failures, small common
samples and wide Monte Carlo intervals as part of the result.

All inputs, numerical diagnostics, warnings and failures are retained in the
ignored study results directory. The script records source revisions and
writes one checkpoint per generated dataset and attempted fit.
